summary: compute_local() returns immediately when host_flag is set without falling back to the CPU implementation, so 'compute gaussian/grid/local/kk' computes nothing at all on any host-only KOKKOS build (and for the /kk/host variant on GPU builds).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:130-132 'if (host_flag) {\n    return;\n  }' with host_flag set at :55 'host_flag = (execution_space == HostKK);'. On a CPU-only Kokkos build LMPDeviceType == Kokkos::DefaultExecutionSpace == LMPHostType (src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:172-173), so ExecutionSpaceFromDevice<LMPDeviceType>::space resolves to the LMPHostType specialisation, HostKK (kokkos_type.h:220-223) -- host_flag is 1 even for the plain '/kk' style. Contrast the sibling port src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:159-160 'if (host_flag) { ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_array();' which does fall back.
failure_scenario: 'lmp -k on t 4 -sf kk' (no GPU) with 'compute g all gaussian/grid/local grid 10 10 10 ...' and 'dump ... local ...' writes zeros in every gaussian column and never sets invoked_local; the non-KOKKOS compute returns the correct densities.
suggested_fix: Replace the bare return with a fallback to the CPU path, e.g. 'if (host_flag) { ComputeGaussianGridLocal::compute_local(); return; }' (syncing x/type to the host first), or port the kernel so it also runs correctly for LMPHostType.

summary: The device kernel drops the compute-group filter, so grid values include atoms outside the compute's group.
failure_scenario: 'group solute type 2' + 'compute g solute gaussian/grid/local/kk grid ...' returns the same densities as a whole-system compute, silently including solvent atoms.
suggested_fix: Add a mask view (sync MASK_MASK in compute_local and store typename AT::t_int_1d_randomread mask) and skip j when '!(mask(j) & groupbit)', matching the CPU loop.

summary: setup() calls ComputeGridLocal::setup() (which allocates alocal with plain memory->create) and then overwrites the alocal pointer with a memoryKK allocation, leaking the first array and leaving gridlocal_allocated=1 so the next setup()'s deallocate() calls memory->destroy() on a Kokkos-backed pointer.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:108-113 'ComputeGridLocal::setup();\n  // allocate arrays\n  memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_alocal, alocal, size_local_rows, size_local_cols, "grid:alocal");'. ComputeGridLocal::setup() (src/ML-SNAP/compute_grid_local.cpp:70-77) calls deallocate(), allocate() -- which sets gridlocal_allocated = 1 and 'memory->create(alocal, size_local_rows, size_local_cols, ...)' (:110-114) -- and assign_coords(). memoryKK->create_kokkos for a value_type** only smallocs the row-pointer array and points array[i] at &data.view_host()(i,0) (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:103-121), while ComputeGridLocal::deallocate() (:121-130) does 'memory->destroy(alocal)' whose T** overload is 'sfree(array[0]); sfree(array);' (src/memory.h:208-214). Modify::setup() calls compute[i]->setup() on every run (src/modify.cpp:301). Note the disabled '//gridlocal_allocated = 0;' left in the KOKKOS destructor at :98. The identical pattern is in src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:146-149, while compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:152 deliberately avoids calling the base setup for exactly this reason.
failure_scenario: An input with two 'run' commands: the first run leaks the base-class alocal; at the start of the second run deallocate() calls free() on &k_alocal.view_host()(0,0), which is not a malloc base pointer -> glibc 'invalid pointer' abort or heap corruption.
suggested_fix: Follow compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h: call ComputeGridLocal::set_grid_global()/set_grid_local() instead of ComputeGridLocal::setup(), do the memoryKK allocation, and fill columns 0-5 yourself; or override allocate()/deallocate() (making them virtual in the base) so only the Kokkos allocation ever exists.

summary: Device kernel calls the C library exp() instead of Kokkos::exp(), against the KOKKOS package rule on device math functions.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:283 'd_alocal(igrid, icol) += static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(d_prefacelem(jtype-1) * exp(-rsq * d_argfacelem(jtype-1)));' inside a KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION; .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4 requires Kokkos::exp in device kernels (compare src/KOKKOS/compute_entropy_atom_kokkos.cpp:300 'Kokkos::exp(...)').
failure_scenario: Compiles today only because ::exp resolves to a CUDA/HIP builtin; it breaks on backends where only the Kokkos wrapper is device-callable.
suggested_fix: Use Kokkos::exp().

summary: d_map is filled by deep-copying an uninitialized host mirror, and d_ninside/max_neighs/inum are allocated or set but never used.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:74 'auto h_map = Kokkos::create_mirror_view(d_map);' is never written (the loop at :76-81 fills only radelem/sigmaelem/prefacelem/argfacelem) yet :86 does 'Kokkos::deep_copy(d_map,h_map);'; d_ninside is reallocated every call at :155 and never read; 'max_neighs = 100;' (:149) and the member 'inum' are dead.
failure_scenario: No wrong results today (d_map is never read), but the copy propagates uninitialized memory and MSan/valgrind will flag it.
suggested_fix: Delete d_map, d_ninside, max_neighs and inum, or initialize h_map before the deep_copy.

summary: FixNVELimitKokkos reads the per-type mass dual view on the device without ever syncing it (there is no MASS_MASK bit and no init() override), so the per-type-mass branch integrates with an uninitialized device mass array.
failure_scenario: GPU build, 'fix 1 all nve/limit/kk 0.1' on a system with per-type masses (no rmass) and no other /kk style that happens to sync k_mass: d_mass holds whatever the freshly allocated device buffer contains (typically zeros), so dtfm = dtf/0 = inf and every velocity becomes NaN on the first half-kick.
suggested_fix: Add an init() override to FixNVELimitKokkos that calls FixNVELimit::init() and then 'atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.template sync<DeviceType>();', exactly as fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:41-47 does.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by rules_C
summary: fix nve/limit/kk reads per-type masses from atomKK->k_mass on the device without ever syncing that DualView (mass has no datamask bit and is only ever modify_host()ed in AtomKokkos), so as the sole integrator on a GPU it divides by zero.
evidence: grep k_mass fix_nve_limit_kokkos.cpp -> only the two view() lines 93 and 167; atom_kokkos.cpp:287-316 modify_host only; correct idiom fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46. Same omission (medium, usually masked by another style's sync) in fix_shake, fix_gravity, fix_momentum, fix_dt_reset, fix_electron_stopping, fix_shardlow kokkos (rules_C).
failure_scenario: fix nve/limit/kk as the only integrator with per-type masses on a GPU: dtfm = dtf/0 -> inf velocities on the first step.
suggested_fix: atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>(); before use (in init()).

summary: fix nve/limit/kk uses atomKK->k_mass on the device without ever syncing the DualView, so per-type masses are read from an uninitialised (zero) device buffer.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_limit_kokkos.cpp:93-101 `auto d_mass = atomKK->k_mass.template view<DeviceType>();` ... `const KK_FLOAT dtfm = l_dtf / d_mass[d_type[i]];` and the same in final_integrate() at lines 167-175.  `grep -n 'k_mass' fix_nve_limit_kokkos.cpp` shows NO `k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()`/`sync_device()` anywhere in the file, and the class overrides only initial_integrate()/final_integrate() (fix_nve_limit_kokkos.h:34-36), so no init() runs a sync either.  atom->mass lives in a DualView that is only ever written on the host: AtomKokkos::allocate_type_arrays (src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:313-316) and every AtomKokkos::set_mass overload (atom_kokkos.cpp:287,293,299,305) call `k_mass.modify_host()` and nothing else.  There is no MASS_MASK in src/atom_masks.h, so `atomKK->sync(execution_space, ...)` can never carry it.  The correct idiom is FixNVEKokkos::init(), src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46: `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();`.
failure_scenario: GPU build, `fix nve/limit/kk` as the only integrator (no fix nve/kk, fix nvt/kk, ... in the input) and per-type masses (no per-atom rmass): the device half of k_mass is the Kokkos default zero-initialised allocation, so `dtfm = dtf/0` is +inf and all velocities/positions become inf/NaN on the first timestep.
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();` (the idiom used by FixNVEKokkos::init(), src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46) before the device view is used.

summary: The maxpartner-overflow retry loop in pre_exchange_no_newton() re-allocates k_partner/k_valuepartner but never re-assigns d_partner/d_valuepartner, so the retry kernel writes past the end of the old (smaller) device views and all collected history is written into a buffer that is then thrown away.
failure_scenario: Granular run (pair gran/hooke/history/kk) in which any atom accumulates more than 8 contact partners: the second pass of the loop writes d_partner(i,m)/d_valuepartner(i,...) beyond the old row stride -- corrupting neighbouring rows and running off the end of the allocation for the last atom -- and the freshly grown k_partner is marked device-modified while containing only the truncated first-pass data, so contact history is silently lost across the atom exchange.
suggested_fix: After both grow_kokkos() calls inside the loop, re-assign d_partner = k_partner.template view<DeviceType>(); and d_valuepartner = k_valuepartner.template view<DeviceType>(); (or simply call grow_arrays(atom->nmax), which already does this).

summary: FixNeighHistoryKokkos does not override pack_restart/size_restart/unpack_restart, so restart files are written from stale host mirrors of npartner/partner/valuepartner and restart data is unpacked into page-allocator chunks that no longer alias the dual views.
evidence: FixNeighHistory sets restart_peratom = 1 / restart_global = 1 and registers Atom::RESTART (src/fix_neigh_history.cpp:41-42, :79-80).  src/fix_neigh_history.cpp:900-907 'void FixNeighHistory::write_restart(FILE *fp) { pre_exchange(); ... }' -- the KOKKOS pre_exchange runs on the device and ends with k_npartner/k_partner/k_valuepartner .modify<DeviceType>() (fix_neigh_history_kokkos.cpp:144-147).  FixNeighHistory::pack_restart (src/fix_neigh_history.cpp:916-927) and size_restart (:979-982) then read npartner[i]/partner[i][n]/valuepartner[i][...] -- the host mirrors -- with no k_*.sync_host().  The KOKKOS class (fix_neigh_history_kokkos.h:44-80) declares no pack_restart/unpack_restart, unlike e.g. FixGJFKokkos which overrides both with sync_host()/modify_host() (src/KOKKOS/fix_gjf_kokkos.cpp:495-511).  Worse, FixNeighHistory::unpack_restart (:934-960) does 'partner[nlocal] = ipage_atom->get(npartner[nlocal]);' -- in the KOKKOS build 'partner' is the row-pointer array that memoryKK->grow_kokkos aliases to k_partner's host mirror (fix_neigh_history_kokkos.cpp:298-300), so this repoints a row away from the dual view and the data is dropped at the next grow_arrays().
failure_scenario: 'write_restart' during a granular run with fix neigh/history/kk: the per-atom contact history written to the file is whatever was last on the host (typically the state from the previous host-side exchange, or zeros), and reading that restart back re-creates contacts with wrong or missing shear history, so the restarted run does not reproduce the original trajectory.
suggested_fix: Override pack_restart/size_restart in FixNeighHistoryKokkos with k_npartner/k_partner/k_valuepartner .sync_host() before delegating, and override unpack_restart to write directly into the dual views' host mirrors (then modify_host()) instead of into ipage_atom/dpage_atom chunks.

summary: post_neighbor()'s kernel writes the masked neighbor index into d_firstflag instead of writing it back into d_neighbors, leaving non-boolean values in the per-neighbor history flag array.
failure_scenario: Today the two ported granular pair styles happen to hide it -- pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.cpp:172 and pair_gran_hertz_history_kokkos.cpp:172 both Kokkos::deep_copy(d_firsttouch,0) at the start of every compute(), so the bogus flags are wiped before pre_exchange reads them.  Any pair style that does not re-zero the flags (or any path where pre_exchange follows post_neighbor without an intervening compute) would count every neighbor as a history partner, immediately overflow maxpartner, and store zero-valued history.
suggested_fix: Change the statement to 'd_neighbors(i,jj) = j;' to mirror the CPU's 'jlist[jj] = j;', and explicitly leave d_firstflag(i,jj) at the 0 written by the preceding deep_copy unless history is found.

summary: d_ncount(ii) is only written for atoms inside the compute group, so atoms outside the group reuse a stale neighbour count from a previous chunk or timestep and get bogus (non-zero) order parameters, where the CPU style memsets their row to zero.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_orientorder_atom_kokkos.cpp:243-292: 'if (mask[i] & groupbit) { ... d_ncount(ii) = ncount; ... }' -- there is no else branch, so d_ncount(ii) keeps its previous contents for out-of-group atoms. The follow-up kernels have no mask test: :298-317 'operator()(TagComputeOrientOrderAtomSelect3, ii) { const int ncount = d_ncount(ii); if ((ncount == 0) || (ncount < nnn)) { zero; return; } if (nnn > 0) { select3(nnn, ncount, ii); ...' and :345-354 BOOP2 likewise. The CPU base zeroes the whole array every call: src/compute_orientorder_atom.cpp:249 'memset(&qnarray[0][0], 0, sizeof(double) * nmax * ncol);' and only computes inside 'if (mask[i] & groupbit)' (:254).
failure_scenario: 'group core type 1' + 'compute q core orientorder/atom/kk degrees 1 6' on a system with more than 'chunksize' atoms (or on any timestep after the first): rows of c_q belonging to atoms of type 2 contain order parameters computed from another atom's stale d_distsq/d_rlist rows instead of the 0.0 the CPU style writes.
suggested_fix: Add 'else d_ncount(ii) = 0;' in the Neigh kernel (or zero d_ncount/d_qnarray before each chunk) so out-of-group atoms take the zeroing path in Select3.

summary: The rmag <= MY_EPSILON early-out skips only the offending neighbour, whereas the CPU calc_boop returns from the whole atom, leaving all its order parameters at zero.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_orientorder_atom_kokkos.cpp:465-468 'const KK_FLOAT rmag = Kokkos::sqrt(...); if (rmag <= MY_EPSILON) { return; }' inside calc_boop1, which handles a single (ii,ineigh) pair, vs src/compute_orientorder_atom.cpp:430-432 'double rmag = sqrt(...); if (rmag <= MY_EPSILON) { return; }' inside the 'for (int ineigh...)' loop of calc_boop -- that return abandons the entire atom, and qn[] stays at the memset zeros.
failure_scenario: Two atoms at (numerically) identical coordinates: the CPU style reports Q_l = 0 for the central atom, the /kk style reports Q_l computed from the remaining neighbours.
suggested_fix: Decide which behaviour is intended and make both styles agree; if the CPU 'return' is itself the bug, fix it to 'continue' there rather than diverging silently.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by group 04
summary: d_ncount(ii) is written only inside 'if (mask[i] & groupbit)' with no else, so atoms outside the compute group keep a stale neighbor count from a previous chunk/timestep and the follow-up kernels compute bogus order parameters for them where the CPU style writes zeros.
evidence: compute_orientorder_atom_kokkos.cpp:243 (group test), 270 (d_ncount(ii) = ncount), no else branch; src/compute_orientorder_atom.cpp memsets qnarray to 0 each call.
failure_scenario: compute orientorder/atom/kk on a subgroup with more than chunksize atoms: out-of-group rows contain garbage instead of 0.
suggested_fix: Add else d_ncount(ii) = 0; (or zero d_ncount/d_qnarray per chunk).

summary: temperature_lookup() copies the table bounds into local `int` variables, truncating them a second time and breaking the `if (t1==hi) delta = -delta;` test that tells the secant solver to search downward from the top of the table.
failure_scenario: A table with hi = 10.5: t1 is clamped to 10 and `t1 == hi` is compared against the int 10, so with a starting temperature at or above the table maximum the solver keeps delta positive and steps t2 = 1.001*t1 further outside the table instead of stepping back inside; energy_lookup then re-clamps and f2-f1 collapses, tripping the 'Secant solver did not converge because table bounds were exceeded' warning path and returning the clamped t1 rather than the correct temperature.
suggested_fix: Declare them as `KK_FLOAT lo = d_table_const.lo(0); KK_FLOAT hi = d_table_const.hi(0);` (together with the view type change in the header).

summary: The dynamic_cast to FixRxKokkos<DeviceType> is not checked for failure, so a fix rx whose KOKKOS instantiation does not match this fix's DeviceType leaves rx_fixKK null and init()/setup()/post_integrate() dereference it.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_eos_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:85 `rx_fixKK = dynamic_cast<FixRxKokkos<DeviceType> *>(rx_fix);` with no null test; it is then dereferenced unconditionally whenever rx_flag is set, at lines 121-122, 185-186 and 239-240 (`rx_fixKK->get_k_species_ind_to_atom_prop_ind()`). The base class only guarantees that rx_fix is a FixRX matching the style regex `^rx/kk` (src/DPD-REACT/fix_eos_table_rx.cpp:57-65), which covers both FixRxKokkos<LMPDeviceType> and FixRxKokkos<LMPHostType>. The sibling style shows the intended guard: src/KOKKOS/fix_dpd_energy_kokkos.cpp:35-37 `pairDPDEKK = dynamic_cast<decltype(pairDPDEKK)>(pairDPDE); if (!pairDPDEKK) error->all(FLERR,"Must use pair_style dpd/fdt/energy/kk with fix dpd/energy/kk");`.
failure_scenario: Mixing suffixes on a GPU build, e.g. `fix r all rx/kk/host ...` together with `fix e all eos/table/rx/kk ...` (device): the dynamic_cast between the two different template instantiations fails, rx_fixKK stays null, and the first call to FixEOStableRXKokkos::init() segfaults instead of printing a diagnostic.
suggested_fix: Add `if (rx_flag && !rx_fixKK) error->all(FLERR,"Must use fix rx/kk with the same suffix as fix eos/table/rx/kk");` right after the cast, following fix_dpd_energy_kokkos.cpp:36-37.

summary: Host-only std::isnan() is called inside the KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION device routine temperature_lookup(), violating the rule that device kernels must use Kokkos:: math.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_eos_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:381-436 is `template<class DeviceType> KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION void FixEOStableRXKokkos<DeviceType>::temperature_lookup(int id, KK_FLOAT ui, KK_FLOAT &thetai) const`.  Line 420: `if (std::isnan(f1) || std::isnan(f2)) k_error_flag.template view<DeviceType>()() = 2;` and line 436: `if (std::isnan(f1) || std::isnan(f2) || std::isnan(ui) || std::isnan(thetai) || std::isnan(t1) || std::isnan(t2))`.  The very same function already uses the portable form on lines 418 and 427 (`if (Kokkos::fabs(f2-f1) < ...)`, `if (Kokkos::fabs(temp-t2) < tolerance)`), so the std:: calls are leftovers.  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4: 'Use Kokkos:: math functions in device kernels ... never std:: -- std::pow and friends fail to compile for GPU targets.'  These are the only std:: math calls inside a device function anywhere in src/KOKKOS (all other std::isnan/std::isinf hits, e.g. pair_uf3_kokkos.cpp:290-543, are in host-side coefficient setup).
failure_scenario: Building the KOKKOS package with DPD-REACT for a CUDA/HIP backend: nvcc/hipcc reject the call to the host-only std::isnan from __device__ code (or silently fall back to the host overload), so `pair_style ... / fix eos/table/rx ... /kk` does not build for GPU.
suggested_fix: Replace every std::isnan(...) in this device routine with Kokkos::isnan(...) (or the `x != x` idiom), matching the Kokkos::fabs() already used two lines above.

summary: DynamicalMatrixKokkos::setup() is never called: the base DynamicalMatrix::setup() is not virtual and DynamicalMatrix::command() calls it non-virtually, so the KOKKOS setup (auto_sync bracketing plus the synced pair->compute) is dead code.
evidence: src/PHONON/dynamical_matrix.h:23 declares 'void setup();' with no 'virtual'.  src/KOKKOS/dynamical_matrix_kokkos.h:35 declares 'void setup();' with no 'override' (it cannot have one).  src/PHONON/dynamical_matrix.cpp, DynamicalMatrix::command(): 'if (style == REGULAR) { setup(); ...' -- an unqualified call inside a DynamicalMatrix member, statically bound to DynamicalMatrix::setup().  The KOKKOS version (src/KOKKOS/dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:91-134) sets 'lmp->kokkos->auto_sync = 1;' for the duration of the domain/comm/neighbor setup, adds an atomKK->sync()/modified() wrapped force->pair->compute(), and clears auto_sync to 0 at the end -- none of which runs.  This is the exact shape of rule 2 in .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md ('Declare virtual void allocate() in the base-class header ... without virtual, the base version is silently called').  src/KOKKOS/third_order_kokkos.cpp:91 has the identical dead override against src/PHONON/third_order.h:23.
failure_scenario: 'dynamical_matrix/kk all regular 0.000001' on a GPU build: the base setup() runs, so lmp->kokkos->auto_sync is left at its default 1 for the whole calculateMatrix() loop and every atomKK->modified() call forces a full host<->device copy of the per-atom arrays -- the KOKKOS command runs at roughly host speed.  Any future correctness fix put into the KOKKOS setup() would also be silently ignored.
suggested_fix: Make DynamicalMatrix::setup() (and ThirdOrder::setup()) virtual in src/PHONON/dynamical_matrix.h / third_order.h and mark the KOKKOS versions 'override'.

summary: DynamicalMatrixKokkos::setup() shadows the non-virtual DynamicalMatrix::setup(), so the KOKKOS version is never executed and the command runs the plain CPU setup path.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/dynamical_matrix_kokkos.h:35 declares `void setup();` with no `override` (only command(), update_force(), force_clear() are override). src/PHONON/dynamical_matrix.h:23 declares `void setup();` NON-virtual (contrast with lines 37-39 `virtual void update_force(); virtual void force_clear(); virtual void openfile(...)`). The only callers are src/PHONON/dynamical_matrix.cpp:169 and :177 inside DynamicalMatrix::command(), which statically binds to DynamicalMatrix::setup(). src/KOKKOS/dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:79-83 `void DynamicalMatrixKokkos::command(...) { atomKK->sync(...); DynamicalMatrix::command(narg, arg); }` -> base command -> base setup. DynamicalMatrixKokkos::setup() (dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:91-133) is therefore dead code; its `lmp->kokkos->auto_sync = 1;` (line 93), the `pair_compute_flag` sync/compute/modified block (lines 117-123) and `lmp->kokkos->auto_sync = 0;` (line 126) never run.
failure_scenario: `dynamical_matrix all regular 0.000001 file dynmat.dat` with -k on -sf kk: DynamicalMatrix::setup() runs instead, so auto_sync is never enabled around domain->pbc()/reset_box()/image_check()/box_too_small_check()/neighbor->build(1), which read the legacy host x/image arrays; on a GPU run those can be stale relative to the device copy, giving wrong ghost/image handling and hence a wrong dynamical matrix (and the KOKKOS-specific pair sync block is silently skipped).
suggested_fix: Declare `virtual void setup();` in src/PHONON/dynamical_matrix.h:23 and mark the KOKKOS one `void setup() override;`, or have DynamicalMatrixKokkos::command() do the setup itself instead of delegating to DynamicalMatrix::command().

summary: ComputeTempSphere::init() detects a temp/region bias with an exact strcmp on tbias->style, which no longer matches once the bias compute is promoted to 'temp/region/kk', so tempbias stays 1 and dof_compute() calls tbias->dof_remove(-1), reading atom->x[-1] out of bounds.
evidence: src/compute_temp_sphere.cpp:106-109 'if (strcmp(tbias->style, "temp/region") == 0) tempbias = 2; else tempbias = 1;'.  src/modify.cpp:1267-1272 rewrites the style string when a suffix is applied: 'std::string estyle = arg[2] + std::string("/") + lmp->non_pair_suffix(); ... compute[ncompute]->style = utils::strdup(estyle);' so the style is literally "temp/region/kk".  src/compute_temp_sphere.cpp:181-182 then takes the tempbias==1 branch: 'if (mode == ALL) dof -= tbias->dof_remove(-1) * natoms_temp;' and src/compute_temp_region.cpp:89-94 'int ComputeTempRegion::dof_remove(int i) { double *x = atom->x[i]; if (region->match(x[0], x[1], x[2])) return 0; return 1; }' dereferences atom->x[-1].  The new src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_region_kokkos.h:16-18 registers temp/region/kk, making this reachable for the first time (there is no /omp or /gpu temp/region).  The identical strcmp appears in ASPHERE/compute_temp_asphere.cpp:122 and BODY/compute_temp_body.cpp:113.
failure_scenario: lmp -sf kk with 'compute b all temp/region myreg' and 'compute t all temp/sphere bias b': the bias compute becomes temp/region/kk, tempbias is set to 1 instead of 2, dof_compute() calls dof_remove(-1) which indexes atom->x[-1] (garbage pointer -> segfault or nonsense), and the per-atom region DOF subtraction is silently skipped so the reported temperature is wrong.
suggested_fix: Compare utils::strip_style_suffix(tbias->style, lmp) with "temp/region" in compute_temp_sphere.cpp (and the same lines in compute_temp_asphere.cpp / compute_temp_body.cpp); optionally also guard dof_remove(-1) in ComputeTempRegion.

summary: FixNVEAsphereKokkos has no superellipsoid guard: it always reads AtomVecEllipsoid's 'bonus' array and derives the inertia from 'shape', but for superellipsoid particles the CPU style uses 'bonus_super[j].inertia' and 'bonus' is never allocated.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style ellipsoid superellipsoid' + 'fix 1 all nve/asphere/kk': the kernel indexes an unallocated/zero-extent k_bonus view -- out-of-bounds device read (illegal memory access on GPU) or, where the view happens to exist, integration with the wrong (shape-derived instead of stored) principal moments of inertia.
suggested_fix: Add the same guard as fix_nve_asphere_noforce_kokkos.cpp:63-65 to FixNVEAsphereKokkos::init(), or port the bonus_super branch.

summary: init_one() fills only the (i,j) element of the self-allocated k_cut_ljsq/k_cut_coulsq dual views, leaving (j,i) at zero, so with more than 12 atom types every pair with itype>jtype loses its entire Coulomb interaction.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_debye_kokkos.cpp:204-207 allocates standalone views 'k_cut_ljsq = DAT::tdual_kkfloat_2d("pair:cut_ljsq",n+1,n+1);' and 'k_cut_coulsq = DAT::tdual_kkfloat_2d(...)', and :253/:255 write only 'k_cut_ljsq.view_host()(i,j) = ...' / 'k_cut_coulsq.view_host()(i,j) = ...'; init_one is only invoked with i<=j (src/pair.cpp:284-288).  src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:245-249 tests 'rsq < c.d_cut_ljsq(itype,jtype)' and 'rsq < c.d_cut_coulsq(itype,jtype)' on the STACKPARAMS=false path, selected when atom->ntypes > MAX_TYPES_STACKPARAMS (pair_kokkos.h:955/969, kokkos_type.h:44 '#define MAX_TYPES_STACKPARAMS 12').  Compare src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_cut_soft_kokkos.cpp:232-234 which correctly assigns both (i,j) and (j,i).
failure_scenario: pair_style coul/debye/kk with 13 or more atom types: for a neighbor pair with itype=7, jtype=2 the cutoff test compares rsq against 0, so compute_fcoul/compute_ecoul are skipped and the screened Coulomb force and energy of that pair are silently zero.
suggested_fix: Assign both elements: 'k_cut_ljsq.view_host()(i,j) = k_cut_ljsq.view_host()(j,i) = cutone*cutone;' and the same for k_cut_coulsq.

summary: Non-atomic writes to the shared scalar d_flag can downgrade a fatal 'Bad FENE bond' (flag 2) to a mere warning (flag 1), so the run continues with a clamped rlogarg instead of aborting.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_fene_kokkos.cpp:200-206 'if (rlogarg < 0.1) { if (rlogarg <= -3.0) d_flag() = 2; else d_flag() = 1; rlogarg = 0.1; }' - plain stores to a single scalar from every thread, no Kokkos::atomic_max. src/KOKKOS/bond_fene_kokkos.cpp:140-143 then does 'if (h_flag() == 1) error->warning(...); else if (h_flag() == 2) error->one(FLERR,"Bad FENE bond");'. The CPU base src/MOLECULE/bond_fene.cpp:89-94 raises 'error->one(FLERR, "Bad FENE bond")' immediately for every bond with rlogarg <= -3.0, so it can never be masked.
failure_scenario: One bond has rlogarg <= -3.0 (thread A writes 2) while another has 0.1 > rlogarg > -3.0 (thread B writes 1). If B's store lands last, h_flag()==1 and the run only warns and keeps integrating a catastrophically stretched bond instead of aborting as the CPU style does.
suggested_fix: Use 'Kokkos::atomic_max(&d_flag(), 2)' / 'Kokkos::atomic_max(&d_flag(), 1)' (or a per-thread reduction into EV/int) so the most severe condition always wins.

summary: build_topology() syncs the device-built bond/angle/dihedral/improper lists to the host only when the corresponding force style has execution_space == Host, but other host-side consumers read neighbor->bondlist through the plain pointer (fix bond/break, compute stress/cartesian, pair mesocnt, the library's neigh_bondlist export) and so see a never-updated host copy.
evidence: neighbor_kokkos.cpp:435-442: 'if (force->bond && force->bond->execution_space == Host) k_bondlist.sync_host();' (same for angle/dihedral/improper). neigh_bond_kokkos.cpp:288 grow_kokkos(k_bondlist,neighbor->bondlist,...) points the plain pointer at the host view; :305 'k_bondlist.modify<DeviceType>()' after the device build, and nothing else syncs it. Host readers with no KOKKOS variant (none of these exist in src/KOKKOS): src/MC/fix_bond_break.cpp:239-245 'int **bondlist = neighbor->bondlist; ... i1 = bondlist[n][0]; i2 = bondlist[n][1]; type = bondlist[n][2];', src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_stress_cartesian.cpp:374-378, src/library.cpp:2345 'return (void *) lmp->neighbor->bondlist' (lammps_extract_global "neigh_bondlist"). neighbor->nbondlist (the count) IS correct on the host (neigh_bond_kokkos.cpp:284), so these loops run over nbondlist rows of stale/zero host data.
failure_scenario: GPU run with bond_style harmonic/kk (device list) plus 'fix bond/break' on a polymer: the fix iterates nbondlist rows whose host contents are zero-initialized (never synced), 'type != btype' skips every row, so no bond is ever broken and no error is raised. A Python/library driver reading neigh_bondlist gets the same stale data. On CPU-only Kokkos builds host and device views alias, so the problem only appears on GPU.
suggested_fix: Sync the topology lists to the host whenever any non-KOKKOS style may read them (simplest: sync when force->bond exists and either execution_space == Host or any fix/compute in modify is not kokkosable), or provide a Neighbor::get_bondlist-style accessor that syncs on demand and route the host consumers through it.

summary: compute_gradients launches its reduction with the default execution space instead of RangePolicy<DeviceType>, so the mliap/kk/host variant of a GPU build runs the kernel on the GPU over host-space views.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_linear_kokkos.cpp:54 'Kokkos::parallel_reduce(data->nlistatoms, KOKKOS_LAMBDA (int ii, double &update) {' -- the integer form of parallel_reduce uses Kokkos::DefaultExecutionSpace, while the views captured on lines 41-49 come from '.template view<DeviceType>()'. The class is instantiated for both device types (lines 94-97 'template class MLIAPModelLinearKokkos<LMPDeviceType>; #ifdef LMP_KOKKOS_GPU template class MLIAPModelLinearKokkos<LMPHostType>;') and the host variant is reachable through 'PairStyle(mliap/kk/host,PairMLIAPKokkos<LMPHostType>)' (src/KOKKOS/pair_mliap_kokkos.h:22), which builds the model with 'new MLIAPModelLinearKokkos<DeviceType>(lmp,arg[iarg+2])' (src/KOKKOS/pair_mliap_kokkos.cpp:180). Every other kernel in this ML-IAP group spells the policy out, e.g. src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.cpp:148,154,186,228 and mliap_descriptor_so3_kokkos.cpp:92,205.
failure_scenario: A CUDA-enabled build running 'pair_style mliap/kk/host model linear ... descriptor so3 ...': the reduction is dispatched to Kokkos::Cuda while d_ielems/d_descriptors/d_betas/d_eatoms are HostSpace views, so the kernel dereferences host pointers on the device (illegal memory address, or silently wrong betas/energy).
suggested_fix: Use 'Kokkos::parallel_reduce(Kokkos::RangePolicy<DeviceType>(0,data->nlistatoms), ...)' as the rest of the ML-IAP Kokkos code does.

summary: PairSNAPKokkosHost declares its virtual overrides without the 'override' specifier, unlike the sibling PairSNAPKokkosDevice.
evidence: pair_snap_kokkos.h:559-563 (Device) 'void coeff(int, char**) override; void init_style() override; double init_one(int, int) override; void compute(int, int) override; double memory_usage() override;' versus :578-582 (Host) 'void coeff(int, char**); void init_style(); double init_one(int, int); void compute(int, int); double memory_usage();'.
failure_scenario: If a Pair base-class signature ever changes, the Host wrapper silently stops overriding and the base implementation is called instead of the KOKKOS one - the compiler cannot warn without 'override'.
suggested_fix: Add 'override' to the five PairSNAPKokkosHost declarations.

summary: snap_dispatch_fused_deidrj_all() sets the policy LaunchBounds from team_size_compute_fused_deidrj but launches with team_size_compute_fused_deidrj_all, so the compiler is told a larger maximum block size than is ever used.
evidence: pair_snap_kokkos.h:273 'SnapAoSoATeamPolicy<DeviceType, team_size_compute_fused_deidrj, TagPairSNAPComputeFusedDeidrjAll> policy_fused_deidrj_all(n_teams_div, team_size_compute_fused_deidrj_all, vector_length);' - the second template argument feeds LaunchBounds (:183-184 'Kokkos::LaunchBounds<vector_length * num_teams>') while the runtime team size is team_size_compute_fused_deidrj_all, which is strictly smaller (e.g. 2 vs 4 for HIP, :107-108, and 2 vs 4 / 1 vs 2 for CUDA, :143-144).
failure_scenario: No wrong numbers, but the kernel is compiled for twice the block size it is launched with, so the register budget per thread (and hence occupancy/performance) is worse than intended.
suggested_fix: Use team_size_compute_fused_deidrj_all as the LaunchBounds template argument for this dispatch.

summary: Eight of the dihedral KOKKOS styles declare Q_MASK in datamask_read although none of them ever reads atom->q, so VerletKokkos performs a needless charge sync around every dihedral compute.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/dihedral_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:44 'datamask_read = X_MASK | F_MASK | Q_MASK | ENERGY_MASK | VIRIAL_MASK;' and the same line in dihedral_class2_kokkos.cpp:45, dihedral_class2xe_kokkos.cpp:46, dihedral_cosine_shift_exp_kokkos.cpp:46, dihedral_cosine_squared_restricted_kokkos.cpp:48, dihedral_fourier_kokkos.cpp:46, dihedral_helix_kokkos.cpp:49 and dihedral_multi_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:45. Grepping those eight .cpp/.h pairs for 'k_q' or 'q[i' returns zero hits -- only dihedral_charmm_kokkos.cpp (line 109 'q = atomKK->k_q.view<DeviceType>();') and dihedral_charmmfsw_kokkos.cpp:116 actually read charge. src/KOKKOS/verlet_kokkos.cpp:173 'atomKK->sync(force->dihedral->execution_space,force->dihedral->datamask_read);' is what consumes the mask. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md requires datamask_read to be 'exactly the per-atom arrays the style reads and writes'.
failure_scenario: No wrong numbers; on a GPU build with a charged system the q dual view is considered part of the dihedral's read set every step, which can force extra host/device traffic and masks a genuine mask error if one is ever introduced.
suggested_fix: Drop Q_MASK from datamask_read in the eight styles that do not touch atom->q, keeping it only in dihedral_charmm_kokkos and dihedral_charmmfsw_kokkos.

summary: None of the 13 KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION declarations in this header carry the required `// NOLINTNEXTLINE` comment.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/pair_bondval_vec_kokkos.h declares e.g. (lines 122-125)
    KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION
    params_bvv() {cut=0;cutsq=0;...};
with no preceding `// NOLINTNEXTLINE`.  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md 'Common mistakes' requires it; pair_adp_kokkos.h:68 and pair_beck_kokkos.h:48 show the expected form.  Among all src/KOKKOS/*.h only pair_bondval_kokkos.h and pair_bondval_vec_kokkos.h (plus bond_quartic_exp, fix_nve_asphere, fix_rigid_small, math_extra) lack it.
failure_scenario: clang-tidy/lint warnings on these declarations.
suggested_fix: Add `// NOLINTNEXTLINE` before each `KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION`.

summary: The 'accelerated styles' line of the atom_style doc page lists only 7 of the 12 atom styles that the KOKKOS package actually provides -- dipole/kk, dpd/kk, ellipsoid/kk, hybrid/kk and sphere/kk are missing.
evidence:
doc/src/atom_style.rst:33:
  * accelerated styles (with same args) = *angle/kk* or *atomic/kk* or *bond/kk* or *charge/kk* or *full/kk* or *molecular/kk* or *spin/kk*
But src/KOKKOS registers 12 AtomStyle /kk variants:
  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_angle_kokkos.h:16 AtomStyle(angle/kk,...)
  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_atomic_kokkos.h:16 AtomStyle(atomic/kk,...)
  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_bond_kokkos.h:16 AtomStyle(bond/kk,...)
  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_charge_kokkos.h:16 AtomStyle(charge/kk,...)
  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_dipole_kokkos.h:16 AtomStyle(dipole/kk,...)      <- undocumented
  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_dpd_kokkos.h:16 AtomStyle(dpd/kk,...)            <- undocumented
  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_ellipsoid_kokkos.h:16 AtomStyle(ellipsoid/kk,...)<- undocumented
  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_full_kokkos.h:16 AtomStyle(full/kk,...)
  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_hybrid_kokkos.h:16 AtomStyle(hybrid/kk,...)      <- undocumented
  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_molecular_kokkos.h:16 AtomStyle(molecular/kk,...)
  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_sphere_kokkos.h:16 AtomStyle(sphere/kk,...)      <- undocumented
  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_spin_kokkos.h:16 AtomStyle(spin/kk,...)
doc/utils/check-styles.py does not check atom styles at all (it only checks command, compute, fix, pair, bond, angle, dihedral, improper, kspace and dump lists, see doc/utils/check-styles.py:316-332), so CI does not catch this.  For comparison, doc/src/region.rst:6 does list all 7 region /kk variants and doc/src/min_style.rst lists all 4 minimizer ones.
failure_scenario: A user reading the atom_style page concludes that 'atom_style sphere' or 'atom_style hybrid' has no KOKKOS variant and either avoids the KOKKOS package for granular/hybrid runs or is surprised when -suffix kk silently selects sphere/kk.
suggested_fix: Extend the list on doc/src/atom_style.rst:33 to *angle/kk*, *atomic/kk*, *bond/kk*, *charge/kk*, *dipole/kk*, *dpd/kk*, *ellipsoid/kk*, *full/kk*, *hybrid/kk*, *molecular/kk*, *sphere/kk*, *spin/kk*.
